title: Focus Stacking for 3D Morphology Analysis in Optical Microscopy
content: Studying materials with complex morphologies often presents challenges for optical microscopy. The technique's shallow depth of field (SDOF) makes it difficult to capture the entire specimen in focus, especially when imaging small objects or intricate structures. Consequently, only a thin section of the image appears sharp when the surface of the sample is not flat. Focus stacking addresses this limitation by acquiring a series of images of the same subject at incrementally adjusted focus distances [1,2]. Specialized software then combines these images, effectively extending the depth of field and producing a single, entirely focused image [3].
